PullRequest.Title: Add Mission Control agent host telemetry and diagnostics
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Complete telemetry and local diagnostics for exposing the native VS Code Agent Host through Mission Control.

- Extend the existing shared connection outcome, first-session-request, and connection-health events to distinguish user-local Mission Control hosts from cloud sandboxes. Reuse upstream connect/recovery reporting rather than adding a parallel event stream; track connected time and unexpected disconnects separately for each environment kind.
- Report host registration and relay lifecycle outcomes, HTTP failures, and unexpected relay losses. Add end-to-end client attempt outcomes so availability failures and the user-local deadline are distinguishable from caller cancellation.
- Attribute successful AHP session creation and existing connection/action/turn telemetry to `mission_control`, alongside SSH and dev tunnels. Prefer the host-known relay route over client metadata and preserve it across reconnects.
- Preserve Web PubSub authentication refresh, keep-alive, and host-configuration isolation for the new Mission Control connection label.
- Log actionable, bounded, credential-redacted HTTP and WPS server messages, connection milestones, and acknowledgement timeouts locally. Keep successful heartbeat and per-frame traffic quiet; do not add server messages, credentials, host names, or addresses to telemetry.

Host diagnostics use `agenthost.log`; client diagnostics use `renderer.log`. The existing telemetry service and consent controls remain authoritative.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed line, standard Fetch implementation, shared call sites, retry schedule, and late 1024-character truncation are directly traced. Exact server error sizes vary, but the uncapped O(bytes) mechanism and its placement before failure/recovery are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Network response bytes, full-body strings, parsed JSON objects, and repeated redaction-string allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is O(error response bytes) per failed register, heartbeat, token, or signing-key request and repeats with check-in recovery retries (500 ms exponential backoff capped at 30 seconds; normal heartbeats run every 60 seconds).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased connection/recovery latency and agent-host CPU, memory, and GC pressure on large non-success responses
Findings.PreviousBehavior: On a non-2xx response, this branch handled credential rejection and threw from the status immediately; it did not drain or parse the response body for diagnostics.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new `await response.text()` drains the entire uncapped body before the failure can propagate, then `JSON.parse` materializes the entire JSON payload and `sanitizeConnectionDiagnosticText` performs multiple whole-string replacements even though only 1024 characters are retained.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The diff replaces the prior immediate `throw new Error(...)` in the non-OK branch with `const text = await response.text()` and full parsing/redaction before throwing, newly moving uncapped response consumption onto every HTTP-failure path.
Findings.Title: Bound the error body before producing diagnostics
Findings.Impact: A verbose JSON error or reverse-proxy HTML response during registration, heartbeat, token refresh, or signing-key recovery now blocks that critical path until the body is downloaded and transformed (up to the request's 15-second abort budget), while creating full-size intermediate allocations. Repeated failed check-ins can repeat the cost and delay Mission Control recovery.
Findings.Evidence: `MissionControlHost` supplies the standard proxy-patched `fetch` with no response-size cap. `_doRequest` is the shared network boundary for register/heartbeat/token/signingKeys, and `_checkIn` awaits it before scheduling recovery; failures back off from 500 ms to 30 seconds. The added line reads the whole `Response`, subsequent lines parse all JSON fields and only then call a sanitizer whose final operation is `.slice(0, limit)`.
Findings.Recommendation: Read only a small bounded prefix from `response.body`, cancel the remainder once the diagnostic cap is reached, and parse/redact only that bounded text while preserving status and validated request ID.

Scenarios.Scenario: Native Agent Host registration, heartbeat, credential refresh, and relay recovery through Mission Control
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration is serialized, then check-in gathers session/policy metadata, awaits register or heartbeat HTTP, optionally fetches token and cached signing keys, and awaits Web PubSub relay readiness. All of those operations must finish before initial readiness or recovery progresses; the newly read non-2xx body is therefore on the failure/recovery critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read or atomically create the persisted Mission Control compute identity
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once during cold configuration, then reused
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same filesystem identity work occurred before the PR

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register/heartbeat/token/signing-key HTTP request through proxy-patched standard Fetch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for the selected check-in operation; additional token/JWKS requests only on expiry/cold cache; retries are serialized
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same HTTP calls existed, but non-2xx status threw without consuming/parsing the body
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial readiness and recovery await it; the diff newly drains and transforms the entire non-2xx body before failure propagates

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish and maintain the Web PubSub relay
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active relay per environment generation; reconnect after loss
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same relay connection existed; the diff adds bounded lifecycle diagnostics
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Relay readiness is awaited before the host is ready

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue Mission Control lifecycle telemetry and local log records
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per selected completion/failure; successful heartbeat/check-in and started events are filtered
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Mission Control operation telemetry or detailed lifecycle log was emitted
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous enqueue/log formatting occurs on completion, with no new remote round trip awaited

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One host environment; normal heartbeat every 60 seconds, recovery retries with 500 ms exponential backoff capped at 30 seconds, signing keys cached for 5 minutes, and one token refresh near expiry. Error-body cost scales with uncapped response bytes and retry count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration uses a Sequencer; `_currentCheckIn` coalesces concurrent check-ins for a generation, so HTTP work is effectively serial per environment. Relay connection is one server per generation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm operation reuses the environment, relay, and signing keys for 5 minutes and refreshes token only near expiry. Cold configuration reads or creates the persisted compute ID and performs register/JWKS/relay setup. Failures are not negatively cached and are retried under bounded backoff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: standard Fetch has no response-size cap, the shared non-OK branch calls `response.text()`, then parses and sanitizes before throwing, and check-in awaits it.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical service error bodies are likely small; large JSON or gateway HTML responses and their prevalence are uncertain. The uncapped allocation and delayed recovery mechanism is direct, so uncertainty affects severity rather than confidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity serialization/allocation regression: cap diagnostic response consumption before parsing/redaction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Renderer connection to a user-local Mission Control host or cloud sandbox
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For user-local hosts, inventory validation awaits getEnvironment/account checks, then the shared connection service mints credentials through connect/reconnect HTTP, stages a Web PubSub transport, completes protocol authentication, and waits for relay establishment. The outer user-local deadline is 60 seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate environment inventory and mint connect/reconnect credentials
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One environment lookup and one credential flow per user action, plus bounded waking polls
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same HTTP calls and ordering existed; the diff adds environment-kind attribution and failure-message decoding
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both complete before relay establishment; no new network call was added by the diff

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renderer IRequestService request forwarding with fully buffered response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per API call
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same full-response buffering occurred before the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Response is already fully buffered before `_connectRequest` receives it

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Web PubSub socket handshake and AHP protocol authentication
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transport per staged connection attempt; policy-controlled reconnects
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same socket path existed; the diff labels user-local transports as Mission Control and applies the existing relay behavior
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection success waits for the handshake/authentication

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue end-to-end attempt and connection telemetry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One attempt event in `finally`, plus existing logical connection events
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dedicated user-local attempt event and environment-kind dimension were absent
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No awaited remote telemetry operation is added

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected environment per connect attempt; waking responses may poll according to Retry-After. Existing live connections are reused, and one in-progress connect is retained per environment ID.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `_connects` prevents duplicate user-local connects for an ID; the shared connection factory tracks one staged connection/address. Reconnect attempts are managed by the protocol client policy rather than fanned out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing live remote connections bypass credential minting. Authentication/account data is reused by existing services; Web PubSub credentials refresh on reconnect. Failed attempts do not become persistent positive cache entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call ordering and boundary cardinality; low incremental performance magnitude for the renderer-only diagnostic parse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure response sizes and waking frequency vary, but renderer responses were already buffered upstream, reducing the incremental cost here to one failure-only decode/parse.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: network/IPC cardinality is unchanged, connects are coalesced per ID, and the response was already buffered before the newly added diagnostic parse.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful AHP session creation and telemetry attribution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing provider session allocation completes first; the diff then looks up the new session summary and synchronously enqueues one telemetry event before returning the createSession response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same provider allocation occurred without the new event
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already awaited before the added telemetry

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Map lookup, summary projection, and telemetry enqueue
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one after each successful allocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous work before response; no added network/IPC await

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation per explicit successful session creation, not discovery or restoration. State lookup is map-backed and summary projection is bounded to one session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new fan-out or limiter change; each protocol request follows existing handler concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session is already present in the authoritative in-memory state map after creation; no cold network/filesystem cache fill is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call placement and map-backed summary lookup are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry backend enqueue implementation cost is not measured, but cardinality is one per user-created session and no scaling collection is copied.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: constant-cardinality work occurs on a low-frequency action after successful creation.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: A timer snapshots each active connection and emits nonzero aggregates; this is off connection establishment and rendering critical paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Telemetry enqueue for aggregate health counters
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero to two events per interval after one scan of active connections
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One combined event could be emitted; the diff separates it into at most two bounded groups
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the user connection critical path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost remains O(active remote connections) per report interval. The result cardinality is bounded to two environment kinds, so at most two health events replace the prior single aggregate event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One interval timer performs a synchronous scan; no parallel boundary burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Counters are reset after each snapshot; disposed connections are removed and cancel the timer when the set becomes empty.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the Map is keyed by the closed union `cloud | user-local` and connection disposal is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The maximum number of simultaneously active remote connections varies, but the scan already existed and grouping key cardinality is fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: same O(connections) scan with constant bounded event fan-out and preserved cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Web PubSub handshake, publish rejection, acknowledgement timeout, and local diagnostics
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Handshake failures prevent readiness; fatal publish rejection or acknowledgement timeout closes the relay. The diff formats sanitized error metadata and writes one warning on these failure paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Web PubSub join/publish frames and acknowledgements
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one join per required group and one acknowledgement per publish; unchanged by the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same WebSocket frames and timeout scheduling existed
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Handshake acknowledgement gates readiness; publish failures terminate the connection

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write sanitized failure diagnostics through VS Code log service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One handshake warning or first/fatal protocol warning, not per frame
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Warnings omitted detailed sanitized server messages
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous formatting/log enqueue on an already failing path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Handshake errors occur once per failed attempt; protocol logging remains first-error-or-fatal, and per-frame traffic is not logged. Error formatting scales with the bounded relay frame/error value on a terminal path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing pending join/publish maps and a single acknowledgement scheduler govern the socket; no new parallel operations are added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; pending acknowledgements are deleted or cleared with transport disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: logging gates and fatal disposal are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Server error-message sizes within relay frame limits vary; these paths are terminal or first-error-only.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: diagnostics are failure-only and cardinality-gated, with no new socket calls or per-frame logging.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 25 changed files and traced native host lifecycle, renderer connection, session creation, periodic aggregation, and relay diagnostics. Submitted one finding for uncapped native Fetch error-body consumption before recovery; all other changed work preserves boundary cardinality or is bounded to constant/low-frequency telemetry and failure logging.
